last_amend_reason: ESC-013 class, amendment 12 — Hank approved this class for amendments 10 and 11 and has since said explicitly not to re-ask for what is already approved. tickets.json verify fields ONLY, TWO tickets, git diff exactly 2 insertions / 2 deletions both on 'verify' lines. T-223 (CRITICAL) and T-224 (HIGH) are the most severe open defects in the project and neither could be SCHEDULED, because swarmloop.py findings writes a placeholder gate into every ticket it mints and red-check correctly refuses it — so the two worst bugs were frozen out of the frontier by bookkeeping rather than by difficulty. THE REPRODUCTIONS NOW EXIST ON main (merge 4bab8fd) and these gates point at them. MECHANISM, measured in both directions before use rather than predicted: each test asserts the CORRECT behaviour and carries @pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True), so a normal run reports '5 xfailed' and 'make verify' returns 'OK: all' — build_succeeds is untouched — while the gate runs the same file with --runxfail and reports '3 failed, 2 deselected' for T-223 and '2 failed, 3 deselected' for T-224, tests genuinely SELECTED, which is exactly what red-check requires and what a bare type-checker gate could not give (that was amendment 11's lesson). strict=True means the fix turns them XPASS, which fails the NORMAL run and forces whoever fixes it to delete the marker, so the scaffolding removes itself instead of rotting. WHAT THE GATES PIN, measured against the real HTTP surface: T-223 cap-100-percent at unit_price 0.001 returns HTTP 201 with fallback false; the same silently; and an UNCAPPED roster row at unit_price 1e-09 returns HTTP 201 as a rankable bid because _is_judged skips the check entirely. T-224 list_price 0.0 with an unparseable store price returns an unauthenticated HTTP 500 out of the middle of an auction, and with a silent store mints a 0.00 rankable fallback offer. No metric, target, acceptance test, product file, dependency or ticket dependency changed.
